summary: OpenAI reports that reinforcement learning scaled on general-purpose reasoning models (o1, an early o3 checkpoint) outperforms a hand-engineered domain-specific competitive-programming system, with o3 achieving an IOI gold medal and an elite-level Codeforces rating without specialized heuristics.

mechanisms.reason: The paper frames scaling general-purpose RL, rather than domain-specific engineering, as the path to state-of-the-art reasoning performance, implying continued investment in RL training compute.
mechanisms.quote: Our findings show that although specialized pipelines such as o1-ioi yield solid improvements, the scaled-up, general-purpose o3 model surpasses those results without relying on hand-crafted inference heuristics.

practices.reason: An early o3 checkpoint is shown to outperform a hand-crafted domain-specific system on coding and reasoning tasks, but the result is the lab's own unreplicated evaluation of a pre-release checkpoint.
practices.quote: when evaluating later models such as o3, we find that o3 achieves gold without hand-crafted domain-specific strategies or relaxed constraints.
